question: Will US inflation fall below 2.5% in any month before January 1, 2027?

model.prompt_context:
Resolution criteria:
- "Yes": Wins if the BLS CPI-U all-items 12-month percent change (not seasonally adjusted), as published in any official BLS Consumer Price Index news release covering a reference month from the period up to and including November 2026, is reported as strictly less than 2.5% in at least one such release whose data falls within the market's eligible window.
- "No": Wins if every BLS CPI-U all-items 12-month percent change (not seasonally adjusted) published in official BLS Consumer Price Index news releases covering reference months up to and including November 2026 is 2.5% or higher.

Clarifications:
- "US inflation" is defined as the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), all items, 12-month percent change, not seasonally adjusted, as stated in the official BLS CPI news release summary.
- Because the December 2026 CPI data is released in January 2027 (after the market's settlement time), only releases covering reference months through November 2026 are eligible.
- The threshold comparison is strictly less than 2.5%; a reading of exactly 2.5% does not satisfy the "Yes" condition.
